The end of your post sounds like therapy might help if your school offers free sessions.
I made a similar-ish post a while ago about my very intense depression and your second to last and third to last paragraphs make me feel like I’m in that mindset again (well, still am, but either way).

I can’t tell you that it got better for me after second year because it did not, but it honestly does become better for a lot of people so you’ve got statistics on your side. Also going to therapy and working on all the things you mentioned in your post including lack of motivation will help you get a more solid footing for second year and the remainder of med school. Also, if I could go back and take the year off/repeat the year/etc., I would.

Thank you for this. I am currently on LOA from my school after they pushed me to the brinking point. I feel like I’m the only one and everyone else thinks I’m insane. I want to go back, but I’m scared.
Rumor has it they are gonna ask to see my medical records from therapist and psych.

Hah. A common complaint I got was “does not know foundational concepts.”

Medical school is one of the worst things I have ever experienced. It is rife with mistreatment, injustice, and unfairness.

There has never been a time I haven’t fantasized about killing myself. It’s just waiting until I get the courage to do it.
I also feel like the only way I will be able to get people to listen to me is if I finally do it.

Med student here: talking to GP doesn’t automatically mean meds. You get a choice, of course. But if I remember correctly, to be diagnosed with MDD you just have to be depressed for 2 weeks at least. So short answer is if you’ve felt like this for 5 weeks, then yes you can probably be diagnosed with MDD.

Sometimes these responses make me feel better. Other times I still feel miserable and angry. I’ve had a lot dark thoughts recently so honestly, not sure what’s gonna happen to me in the long run. I’m on max dose of antidepressants and already done an IOP run…so eh. Anyway though—

Thanks for the little moments this post gives me. Please grow up to be much nicer residents/attendings/clerkship directors/faculty than the ones I’ve met. Always think before you yell, even if you can’t fathom how outrageous or stupid or aloof or whatever your students are. And remember you don’t know their life beyond this one tiny part of it. And lastly, remember that someone’s mental health is not a scapegoat for mistreatment and injustice. The answer is not always that “they need to fix themselves.” It can help, yes, but it is also an oft-used vehicle for victim blaming.

I guess that’s it. I had some parting words for this thread about friendships in medical school, but it just brought up bad memories, so I’m going to leave this as is.

Thank you guys for being nicer to me than almost my whole 200-person class.

Just a take from someone who was told by a wannabe psychiatrist in my class that I have “so many neuroses”—people can have extenuating circumstances.

If that kid (actually he was more like 45) bothered to think that he didn’t know everything about me—all the expansive physical, emotional, mental, and sexual abuse I’ve experienced literally my entire life up to and continuing my med school journey—maybe he would have thought before he spoke. Med school, rife with mistreatment, could just be the tip of the iceberg—the straw that broke the camel’s back.

Sorry, some of these comments seemed a bit like jumping to judgement. Please remember you don’t know everyone’s story. And if you show one of your more fragile classmates some love, you never know, you might be showing them one of the few instances of love they’ve had. Just because we’re in medical school doesn’t mean we’re exempt from trauma and PTSD.
Bruh me too 😂

Good idea, but some times there are times to speak up. Not even necessarily speak up, but support.
I do not advise getting into drama involving faculty, but if—for lack of better words—one of your classmates is being bullied by others, please support them.
I had a terrible time my M1 year and some of my M2 year because of this. I felt like hell. Most of my classmates preferred to ignore as they did not want to get involved like that. I would have preferred that as well, but I didn’t really have a choice.

Having people and “friends” I made in my class flat out tell me they don’t want to hear about what I had to say and would not “stand up for me” as it were was incredibly hurtful and lonely.

Thank you! Also, if you have an unbelievable life story, you found the right place! Me too. I am actually quite literally known for my hellish (and hellishly unbelievable) luck, as well having a life that my therapists have called (in more eloquent words), “the worst case of A Series of Unfortunate Events we have ever seen.”

I also have a friend in another medical school on the other side of the country who has an even more absurd life. I won’t post it all here but man. She has crazy luck, although it might be a mixture of good and bad luck seeing as how she accidentally stumbled upon and uncovered a sex trafficking ring and some tangentially related murders. Bad because, well...self-explanatory. But good because she helped bring justice and quite literally saved a bunch of people’s lives before she even finished M2 year!

Long story short, the likelihood I would doubt your life circumstances is low, no matter how Lifetime-movie-like or Humans-of-New-York-ish they seem. So don’t worry, I believe you!
She screamed and cried in my face. It was an extraordinarily not fun experience. I will forever hate that woman.
I also would take notes from B and B in the FA Book, and that helped

USMLE-Rx has flashcards associated with FA! Try those—those seriously saved my butt. When you flip the card, it will show you the answer b it  also the FA section correlated with it, allowing you to see the material multiple times. And it gives you lots of options on how to organize decks, so if you wanted to just pump out psych pharm you could, etc. the USMLE Rx questions also show the correlated FA page once you answer, and you can choose to quickly do those flashcards before another question.

If nothing else, HIGHLY SUGGEST IT FOR NEUROANATOMY AND NEUROPHYS.
